transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. 

Um, well, I'm here because things kind of went off the rails at work recently. I work in human resources, and... I pushed ahead with this new onboarding launch we were planning. I ended up committing company money and a lot of vendor time before any of the actual approvals were in place. 

At the time, it just felt... bold, I guess? Like it was absolutely necessary to just take charge and get it moving. But now... well, now I'm on administrative leave, and everyone is asking me what I was thinking. So I guess I'm here to figure that out.
During that time when you felt so bold, did you experience any unusual beliefs or perceive things that others around you did not seem to notice?

No, um, nothing like that. I didn't see or hear anything that wasn't there, if that's what you mean. And I didn't have any strange beliefs... I didn't think I had superpowers or anything. 

I just... I really thought my plan was brilliant and that the executives would thank me once it was done. So, no, everything around me was normal, I just felt incredibly confident about what I was doing.
During that time when you were pushing ahead with your plan, did you feel like you had significantly more energy or needed much less sleep than usual?

Yeah, I definitely had a lot more energy. Um, it actually felt almost impossible to just sit at my desk. It was like my body had a motor in it. I kept arriving at the office really early, and then I'd just be walking the floors, rewriting all the presentation decks, emailing people, and rearranging plans. I just couldn't stop moving and doing things.
Have you ever experienced a significant period in the past where you felt the exact opposite of this—like you were profoundly sad, had no energy, or felt hopeless for weeks at a time?

No, um... I don't think I have. I mean, I get stressed or have a bad day here and there, like anyone, but... no, nothing like what you're describing. I've never gone through a time where I felt hopeless or had no energy for weeks on end.

During that period of high energy, did you experience any other major consequences, such as being hospitalized or becoming so disorganized that you were completely unable to function in your daily life?

No, I wasn't hospitalized or anything like that. I mean, obviously, I ended up getting fired because of what I did at work, but... I wasn't completely unable to function. I was actually functioning a lot, maybe too much. I was getting to work, doing all those things I mentioned. I just... I took it too far and crossed lines I shouldn't have. But no hospital, no.
How many days in a row did this period of high energy and feeling like you had a motor in your body last?

Well, it didn't just happen for a few days. It's actually been building up for about a month now. It all started around the time this new executive came in and began challenging the onboarding redesign I was working on. So yeah, it's been going on for a solid month.
During this past month when you felt so energetic, did you have periods where you felt particularly irritable, or perhaps unusually sensitive to rejection or criticism?

Yeah, I've definitely had moments like that. For the past few weeks, it's been... well, I've felt either brilliantly alive, like I was finally going to show leadership what HR can really be, or I'd get suddenly furious. If someone questioned me, even over really small things like minor edits or just routine budget questions, I would just get incredibly mad. So, yes, the irritability was definitely there.

Have you ever gone through periods, perhaps lasting a few days at a time, where you felt 'down,' less productive, or less interested in things, even if it didn't reach the level of a full-blown depression?

No, I... I don't think so. I haven't really noticed feeling down or losing interest in things like that. Usually, I'm just kind of steady, or... well, like I've been this past month with all that extra energy. But I haven't had days where I just felt low or unproductive, no.
Looking back over the last few years, have you ever had other periods, perhaps lasting a few days or weeks, where you felt similarly energetic, productive, or 'on a roll'?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had times where I felt good about a project or got a lot done, but... nothing like this. This past month has been totally different from how I normally operate. So, no, I haven't really had other periods like this one before.
